title: Chapter 22: Murder by Midnight
html:
Chen Ge covered his mouth before a sound could escape. The instant he understood what he was seeing, he sent He San a message: “Call the police. Now.”

The stairwell was dark, and a door separated Chen Ge from the others, so his viewers could not see what was happening. He had no attention to spare for the stream anyway. He watched through the narrow gap without moving.

There really is someone hidden in the wall. That’s what they came up here to move.The tenants were only a few steps away. If any of them entered the room where he was hiding, he would be discovered immediately.

“At this rate we’ll be here all night,” the landlord muttered, moving forward to help. The group worked as quietly as they could, clearly trying not to alert anyone else in the building.

Dust drifted through the corridor as they worked. Everyone looked tense and uncomfortable, and their lack of experience made the process slow and awkward.

After some time, they managed to remove what had been concealed in the wall and wrapped it for transport.

“You stay and clean up,” the landlord told the heavyset man. “The rest of us will take this away.”

“I’m coming with you!” the man blurted out. The ordeal had left him badly shaken, and he clearly had no intention of remaining alone on the third floor.

“Can you stop panicking for five minutes?” The landlord turned to the woman. “Juan Er, stay here with him. Meet us at the usual place afterward.”

The landlord and the tattooed man then carried the bundle downstairs.

Because of the landlord’s limp, his footsteps fell in an uneven rhythm. As he passed the room where Chen Ge was hiding, he suddenly stopped.

“Why is there so much stuffing on the floor?”

Chen Ge’s heart lurched. When he had opened the dolls, bits of stuffing and paper had fallen without him noticing. It had been too dark to see the mess, and now there was nothing he could do about it.

“Probably just rubbish,” the tattooed man said from behind him. “We’ll deal with it later. Let’s finish the important part first.” The landlord hesitated, then continued toward the stairs.

“Don’t just stand there. Clean this up.” The woman and the heavyset man quickly straightened the area and gathered what remained before leaving as well.

Their footsteps gradually faded. Only when the third floor had been silent for a while did Chen Ge finally breathe again. He peered through the gap. The corridor was dark and empty.

Damn. That was close.

He waited several more minutes to make sure no one was returning. Then he slipped out from behind the door and moved carefully through the darkness.

From what they said, those people are certainly hiding crimes of their own—but the person concealed in the wall doesn’t seem to be one of them.

The situation was twisted. After taking control of the old man’s property, the group had discovered evidence of an older crime they had nothing to do with. Any ordinary tenant would have called the police, but they were all hiding offenses of their own. Instead, fear of investigation had pushed them into concealing someone else’s secret as well.

No wonder the landlord kept warning me not to wander around after dark.

As his eyes adjusted, Chen Ge moved faster. He no longer cared about retrieving his backpack; he only wanted to get out of the building.

Damn it.

The front door was locked. He was trapped inside.

They even locked the building behind them?A fresh wave of anxiety tightened in his chest.The lower windows are secured, and the third floor is sealed up. There has to be another way out from the second floor.

The longer he remained inside Ping An Apartments, the worse his unease became. He headed back upstairs, and in the darkness the corridor seemed to stretch like the throat of some enormous creature.

It’s too quiet.His room sat beside the landlord’s at the far end of the corridor. Every closed door now looked threatening. Holding his breath, Chen Ge made his way toward Room 208.

No one came out. Good. I just need to find a way out from one of these rooms.He reached for his key, but the moment he looked at the lock, his hand froze.

Where is the marker I left?

Every hair on his body seemed to rise at once. Fear washed over him, leaving him rooted to the spot.

Someone entered my room. They know I wasn’t inside.

His breathing quickened, cold dread settling in his chest.

When did it happen? While I was upstairs? After they noticed the stuffing?The answer no longer mattered. Chen Ge backed away from the closed door and forced himself to think.I can’t go in. Someone could be waiting for me.

Whatever panic he felt, one fact was clear: he needed to get out of the building. He retreated without making a sound, searching the second floor for another route.

He moved toward the far end of the corridor, putting as much distance as possible between himself and Room 208.

I underestimated these people. I need an exit—now.With no time left to hesitate, Chen Ge forced open an unoccupied room at the far end of the corridor.

The sudden noise shattered the silence of Ping An Apartments. Almost immediately, doors opened behind him.

Room 208 flew open. The landlord and the tattooed man rushed into the corridor, their expressions making it clear that Chen Ge had been discovered.

Come on!

The empty room finally opened to him, and Chen Ge bolted inside.
